data.title: Therapeutic Immune Reprogramming by Rapamycin Attenuates Plaque Inflammation and Lymphoid Immune Responses in Aged Atherosclerotic Mice
data.authors: de Mol J; de Korte DH; Depuydt MAC; Smit V; Kleijn MNAB; van Santbrink PJ; Binder CJ; Porsch F; Schaftenaar FH; Foks AC

evidence.label: Animal model
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

data.model_system: Aged (80-90 wk) male Ldlr-/- mice with established atherosclerosis; rapamycin i.p. triweekly x 8 weeks vs. control
data.finding: In aged atherosclerotic mice, rapamycin (mTORC1 inhibition) reduced plaque macrophage content and total T cell numbers, shifted CD8 T cells from effector to central-memory phenotype, enriched aortic regulatory T cells (higher Foxp3/Tgfb1), reduced Tfh cells, germinal-center B cells, plasma cells and autoantibody levels, diminished age-associated B cells, and lowered senescence-enrichment scores in aortic leukocytes -- consistent with rapamycin acting as an immune-rejuvenation therapeutic that mitigates age-related atherogenic inflammation.
data.abstract_excerpt: Aging is a major risk factor for atherosclerosis and is accompanied by profound changes in the immune system, including effector T cell expansion, senescent cell accumulation, and increased pro-inflammatory signaling. Rapamycin, a promising rejuvenation therapeutic that inhibits mTORC1 and modulates immune aging, was investigated for its potential to attenuate pro-atherogenic immune responses in aged atherosclerotic mice. 80- to 90-week-old male Ldlr-/- mice with established atherosclerotic lesions were treated intraperitoneally with rapamycin or control triweekly for 8 weeks.
